findings.title: Feature-disabled branch is only covered for the metadata subcommand
findings.body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled covers only UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME, but the identical gating block was added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (quarkus/runtime/.../UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java line 46-50). There is no test that verifies the `check` subcommand also prints 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature `rolling-updates` is not enabled.' and exits with code FEATURE_DISABLED (4). If someone removes or alters the feature check in UpdateCompatibilityCheck, this test suite will not notice. Add a sibling @Launch test (e.g. testFeatureNotEnabledCheck) that invokes the check subcommand without ENABLE_FEATURE and asserts both the error message and the exit code.

findings.title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changed from 4 to 3
findings.body: Before this PR, RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was 4, so external CI/GitOps scripts invoking `kc.sh update-compatibility check` would observe exit code 4 when a recreate upgrade was required. This PR redefines it to 3 and reassigns 4 to the new FEATURE_DISABLED case. Any automation that checks `if exit_code == 4 then recreate` will silently misinterpret the new exit code 4 as "recreate required" when in reality it now means "rolling-updates feature is disabled". The change is reflected in update-compatibility.adoc, but the docs do not call out the re-numbering of the previously documented exit code 4; users running older guides will not realize the semantics of 4 have changed. This deserves an explicit migration note (e.g., "previously 4 meant recreate; in this release 3 means recreate and 4 means feature-disabled") and should be flagged in the release notes / changelog so existing scripts can be updated.

findings.title: CAUTION contradicts the documented default behavior and the operator tests
findings.body: The new CAUTION block states: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' Immediately below, the NOTE block (line 461-466) explains the default behavior ('the update strategy defaults to mimicking Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior') which works without enabling the feature. The accompanying test in UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment deliberately does NOT enable ROLLING_UPDATES when updateStrategy is null, and testImageChange(null) asserts that the default recreate-on-image-change flow still works without the feature. So the operator does NOT fail without the feature when the user sticks to default behavior; it only fails when the user attempts to set spec.update.strategy. The CAUTION is misleading and contradicts both the NOTE and the test. It should be reworded to make it clear the feature is only required to use spec.update.strategy, not for the operator to function at all.

findings.title: Enabled feature is not asserted to be actually applied to the running deployment
findings.body: createInitialDeployment sets kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey())), but the tests (testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount) only assert on upgrade status conditions - they never verify that the rolling-updates feature is present in the CR that the operator processed (e.g. by asserting on the persisted CR or by checking that the StatefulSet was/wasn't recreated according to the documented semantics). If the operator ever silently drops the featureSpec on submit, these tests would still pass. Adding at least one assertion like `assertThat(currentKc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().getEnabledFeatures()).contains("rolling-updates")` would close this gap and would also detect regressions in the CR schema mapping introduced by the FeatureSpec/UnsupportedSpec refactor in this PR.
